Action Plan:
1. Provide electronic prescriptions within the hour for:
   • Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
   • Clenil Modulite (beclomethasone) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
   • Oral steroid tablets (name/dose not documented) – 2 tablets each morning for 5 days.  
2. Supply a spacer device and instruct patient on correct use (2 puffs to prime, breathe in/out through spacer for 5–10 breaths).  
3. Education: continue Clenil daily once recovered; use Salbutamol PRN; if Salbutamol needed more frequently than every 3 hours or symptoms worsen (increasing SOB, chest tightness, light-headedness), seek urgent medical review.  
4. Advise rest and allow self-certified sick leave for up to 7 days; clinician note can be provided if symptoms persist.  
5. Arrange follow-up if no improvement after steroid course or earlier if deterioration.  
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: 3-hour history of tight chest with mild shortness of breath, wheeze, non-productive cough.  
• Recent history: Viral URTI last week (runny nose, sore throat); cough persisted.  
• Past medical history: Asthma (severe exacerbation requiring intubation age 16-17); hay fever; childhood eczema; childhood milk protein allergy (resolved).  
• Medications:  
  – Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – currently out; not used past week.  
  – Clenil Modulite inhaler – currently out; not used past week.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies; environmental allergies to dust.  
• Family history: Mother – eczema; Father – asthma.  
• Social history: University student; no further details provided.

Objective:
• Remote consultation – no physical examination performed.  
• Patient reports:  
  – Not short of breath at rest.  
  – Mildly more breathless on stair climbing than baseline.  
  – No chest pain, only tightness.  
  – No productive sputum.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute asthma exacerbation  
   - Assessment: Likely viral-triggered asthma flare compounded by 1-week lapse in preventer/reliever use.  
   - Investigations: None indicated during telehealth call.  
   - Treatment: Restart Salbutamol PRN; restart Clenil Modulite regularly; 5-day course of oral steroids; provide spacer; asthma action advice given.  
   - Referrals: None at present; advised to seek in-person review if deterioration.

2. Medication refill (Salbutamol, Clenil, spacer)  
   - Assessment: Out-of-stock inhalers contributing to inadequate asthma control.  
   - Treatment: Electronic prescriptions sent to pharmacy; spacer supplied.

3. Sick leave / recovery advice  
   - Assessment: Patient symptomatic and may benefit from rest away from work.  
   - Treatment: Advised self-certify first 7 days; clinician can issue fit note if needed.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: No vital signs, peak flow, or objective respiratory exam documented; steroid name/dose not specified.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; brief audio dropouts but meaning preserved.
